analysis.title: Up and Adam (Investment Strategy daily, Wednesday, October 14, 2026)
key_insights: The S&P 500 Semiconductor Index has fallen to a one-month low and is essentially flat since May. The S&P 500 Software Index is at its highest level since October 2025. Raymond James reads this as investor focus moving from AI infrastructure to software firms that monetize AI applications, and stays positive on the Technology sector overall.

The Cass Freight Index, a gauge of North American shipping volumes, rose YoY in both August and September after 42 months of YoY declines. Higher freight volumes point to higher diesel demand, which helps explain why diesel prices are up more YTD than oil.

Expensive diesel is weighing on transport firm earnings, but Raymond James expects diesel prices to moderate. With the S&P 500 Industrials sector down 9.5% from recent highs, it views the pullback as a buying opportunity.

September CPI is released at 8:30 AM ET. Raymond James expects headline CPI +0.45% MoM (3.45% YoY), boosted by energy as WTI crude averaged $97/barrel, the highest monthly average since May. It expects core CPI +0.2% MoM (2.4% YoY) because pass-through into broader components is limited.

Raymond James shares the Fed's approach of looking past temporary commodity price spikes while core inflation stays contained. A moderate CPI print plus a healthy labor market would support the Fed holding rates steady on October 27-28.

Big bank earnings reinforce the view that consumer spending is strong. Credit card sales volumes were up 13% YoY at Citigroup, 12% at Wells Fargo and 10% at JP Morgan, and card charge-off rates fell at all three despite gasoline prices near post-COVID highs.

Consensus expects MSCI Europe to post a second straight quarter of double-digit YoY EPS growth in 3Q earnings season. Energy is estimated to generate about 50% of that growth while making up about 5% of market cap.

Raymond James expects oil prices to decline over the next 12 months, so narrow earnings breadth in Europe could become a headwind. Among developed markets it continues to favor the US and Japan over Europe.

sector_views.rationale: Leadership is shifting from semiconductors to software, but the AI megatrend needs both hardware and software, so Raymond James stays positive on the sector overall.

The sector is down 9.5% from recent highs and freight volumes are turning positive after 42 months of YoY declines. Raymond James views the pullback as a buying opportunity and expects diesel prices to moderate.
Earnings growth is narrowly concentrated in Energy, which Raymond James expects to fade as oil prices decline. It favors the US and Japan over Europe.

earnings_insights: Citigroup credit card sales volumes +13% YoY, Wells Fargo +12%, JP Morgan +10% (reported in the 3Q big bank earnings). Card charge-off rates declined at all three.

MSCI Europe 3Q consensus: second straight quarter of double-digit YoY EPS growth (consensus estimate, not yet reported). Energy is estimated to contribute about 50% of the EPS growth versus about 5% of market cap.
